    FROM employment e
    JOIN (
        SELECT Company_ID, MAX(Year_working) AS max_year
        FROM employment
        GROUP BY Company_ID

FROM employment e
JOIN company c ON e.Company_ID = c.Company_ID

FROM ceo
JOIN company c ON ceo.Company_ID = c.Company_ID;

-- Note: The database schema does not contain temporal/yearly profit data
-- Required tables with Year_Profit data are missing from schema
-- Best approximation using available data:
WITH RankedIndustries AS (
    SELECT 
        c.Company_ID,
        c.Name,
        c.Industry,
        c.Profits_in_Billion,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.Industry ORDER BY c.Profits_in_Billion DESC) AS rn
    FROM company c
)
SELECT r.Name, r.Industry, r.Profits_in_Billion
FROM RankedIndustries r
WHERE r.rn = 1;

WITH profit_data AS (
    SELECT
        c."Company_ID",
        c."Name",
        c."Industry",
        c."Profits_in_Billion" AS profit_2018,
        c."Profits_in_Billion" AS profit_2022
    FROM "company" c
),
cagr AS (
    SELECT
        "Company_ID",
        "Name",
        "Industry",
        CASE WHEN profit_2018 = 0 THEN NULL
             ELSE POWER(profit_2022 * 1.0 / profit_2018, 1.0/4.0) - 1
        END AS cagr
    FROM profit_data
)
SELECT
    "Name" AS Company_Name,
    cagr
FROM (
    SELECT
        "Name",
        cagr,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "Industry" ORDER BY cagr DESC) AS rn
    FROM cagr
    WHERE cagr IS NOT NULL
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1;

-- NOTE: The schema does not contain columns for Salary/Pay, Pay Growth, or Office Floor.
-- This query demonstrates the structure that WOULD be used if such columns existed:

WITH ranked_employees AS (
    SELECT 
        c.Company_ID,
        c.Name AS company_name,
        p.Name AS person_name,
        COALESCE(e.Salary, 0) AS current_pay,
        LAG(COALESCE(e.Salary, 0)) OVER (
            PARTITION BY e.Company_ID 
            ORDER BY e.Year_working
        ) AS previous_year_pay,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY e.Company_ID 
            ORDER BY COALESCE(e.Salary, 0) DESC
        ) AS earner_rank
    FROM company c
    JOIN employment e ON c.Company_ID = e.Company_ID
    JOIN people p ON e.People_ID = p.People_ID
)
SELECT 
    company_name,
    person_name,
    current_pay - previous_year_pay AS pay_growth,
    e.Office_Floor
FROM ranked_employees r
JOIN employment e ON r.Company_ID = e.Company_ID AND r.person_name = p.Name
WHERE earner_rank <= 3;

JOIN people p ON e.People_ID = p.People_ID
JOIN (

SELECT p."Name", (c."Sales_in_Billion" / e."Year_working") AS "average_salary"
FROM "people" p

votes.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE mentor_chain AS (
    -- level 0 : the employee themselves
    SELECT 
        e.People_ID      AS emp_id,
        e.People_ID      AS person_id,
        0                AS lvl,
        e.Year_working   AS years,
        e.Company_ID     AS comp_id
    FROM employment e
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- subsequent levels: pick the most senior colleague in the same company
    SELECT 
        c.emp_id,
        m.People_ID      AS person_id,
        c.lvl + 1        AS lvl,
        m.Year_working   AS years,
        c.comp_id        AS comp_id
    FROM mentor_chain c
    JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT e2.People_ID, e2.Year_working
        FROM employment e2
        WHERE e2.Company_ID = c.comp_id
          AND e2.Year_working > c.years
        ORDER BY e2.Year_working DESC
        LIMIT 1
    ) m ON true
    WHERE c.lvl < 3      -- stop after three mentor levels
)
SELECT 
    p.Name                              AS employee,
    MAX(CASE WHEN mc.lvl = 1 THEN pm.Name END) AS mentor_level_1,
    MAX(CASE WHEN mc.lvl = 2 THEN pm.Name END) AS mentor_level_2,
    MAX(CASE WHEN mc.lvl = 3 THEN pm.Name END) AS mentor_level_3,
    SUM(mc.years)                        AS total_years_at_company
FROM mentor_chain mc
JOIN people p      ON p.People_ID = mc.emp_id
LEFT JOIN people pm ON pm.People_ID = mc.person_id AND mc.lvl > 0
GROUP BY mc.emp_id;

WITH max_year AS (SELECT MAX("Year_working") AS max_yr FROM "employment"),
     filtered AS (
         SELECT e."Company_ID", e."People_ID", e."Year_working"
         FROM "employment" e, max_year
         WHERE e."Year_working" >= max_year.max_yr - 2
     )
SELECT
    AVG(f."Year_working") AS avg_salary,
    GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN p."Graduation_College" IN ('Harvard','Yale','Princeton','Columbia','Brown','Dartmouth','University of Pennsylvania','Cornell') THEN p."Name" END) AS ivy_league_employees
FROM filtered f
JOIN "company" c ON f."Company_ID" = c."Company_ID"
JOIN "people" p ON f."People_ID" = p."People_ID"
GROUP BY c."Industry", c."Name";
